name: custom-eq
title: Custom EQ
summary: Adds your own EQ to Settings > EQ.
details: A new item "Custom" shows in Settings > EQ.

Set the sliders in this pane, then flash the iPod. The default is 3 bands. The Simple view has Bass, Mids and Treble. The Advanced view gives each band a type, a frequency and Q. To change the bands, flash the iPod again.
Export EQ makes a small .ipodeq file that you can send to another person. Import EQ reads the file. The iPod changes when you flash it.
Start From Apple Preset sets the bands close to an Apple preset. You can then change them.
Use All 5 Bands adds Warmth and Clarity. Apple never uses more than 3 bands in one EQ, so you must agree to a warning first.
The patch uses the EQ of the iPod. A band at 0 dB is off and uses no CPU time.
The EQ operates as the Apple presets do. A strong boost can distort loud music.
Prevent Clipping lowers the level by the highest boost. The music does not distort, but it sounds quieter.
notes: The iPod applies the EQ only to 16-bit music at 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz. The Apple presets have the same limit.
The name "Custom" is in English in all languages.
This is a test version. A setting with 4 or 5 active bands is not tested on a real iPod.

steps: Set a strong bass boost in this pane. Flash the iPod.
On the iPod, go to Settings > EQ and select Custom.
Play a song with headphones. Change between Custom and Flat. The bass must change.
Turn on Use All 5 Bands and set all the sliders. Flash the iPod again.
Play MP3, AAC and Apple Lossless songs. Make sure that the music has no gaps.
